decisions.handoff: #39 runs the final 3x100k resource soak against this configuration.
decisions.rationale: It preserves the measured fixed topology and fresh-store isolation; this archive introduces no runtime behavior change.

decisions.candidate: bounded preparation/cache reuse versus cold preparation
decisions.handoff: #9 generalizes the cache key, policy, eviction, and multi-component compatibility proof.
decisions.rationale: The cache is node-owned, bounded, and stores prepared immutable state only; stores and instances remain fresh per activation.
decisions.scope: retain existing bounded one-entry prepared-component cache

decisions.handoff: #8 owns configuration, fairness, and fixed multi-class capacity policy.
decisions.rationale: The matrix measures fixed ratios without selecting a universal winner. Only 3 matched candidate runs are retained; Phase 0 requires at least 7 comparable runs before a faster result can justify adoption.

decisions.handoff: #9 must provide generalized pooling limits, density evidence, and a reset/isolation proof before any production choice.
decisions.rationale: The experiment has an explicit fixed upper bound and no retained linear-memory allowance, but it changes node-fixed mapping and reset behavior. Only 3 matched candidate runs are retained; Phase 0 requires at least 7 comparable runs before a faster result can justify adoption.

decisions.handoff: #9 owns target-aware Wasmtime policy and must retain a safe non-COW fallback.
decisions.rationale: Linux support is profiled explicitly, but its parallel-memory tradeoff is workload-dependent. Only 3 matched candidate runs are retained; Phase 0 requires at least 7 comparable runs before a faster result can justify adoption.

decisions.candidate: avoidable activation-path allocations and payload copies
decisions.handoff: #9 owns canonical value mapping; #11 owns activation-envelope/lifecycle ownership and cleanup.
decisions.rationale: Heaptrack evidence and source-attribution maps identify the current boundaries, but removing copies before the Phase 1 generic value codec and lifecycle shapes exist risks changing contracts or attribution.

decisions.candidate: store/instance reuse, persistent AOT artifacts, compiler caches, snapshots, and native execution
decisions.handoff: Trusted AOT supply-chain work is Phase 2; fresh stores and instances remain mandatory in #9.
decisions.rationale: These candidates require a new reset/isolation or provenance proof and are forbidden from silently entering Phase 0.
